areaPack.howToEdit: RUNTIME CONTENT. Three tiers. Held claim·reason·source identical.

meta.title: Silver City — Papyrus Vault
meta.subtitle: Ancient Egyptian Sands Reveal the Earliest Pages of Christ's Gospels
meta.blurb: Skeptics claim the story of Jesus Christ was invented centuries later like a long game of telephone. Step into the Papyrus Vault to inspect the oldest surviving New Testament pages pulled from desert sands, proving the Gospels were written, copied, and read across the Roman world from the earliest generations.
meta.notes: Unlock after Iron Spike Way. Objection: The Gospels about Jesus Christ were invented hundreds of years later as evolving folklore.

learn.shortStory: In a quiet Egyptian village, an early believer treasured a papyrus scrap of John chapter 18. Centuries later, scholars discovered this fragment, realizing it was written just decades after John lived. It utterly crushed claims that the Gospel of Jesus Christ was invented centuries later.

learn.shortStory: A faithful craftsman stitched papyrus leaves together along the Nile to make a durable codex. This booklet gathered Paul's letters so local congregations could study the deity and resurrection of Jesus Christ together. Its survival shows believers cherished these teachings as Scripture.
learn.mainIdea: Papyrus P46 proves Christians collected letters honoring Jesus Christ around 200 AD.
learn.gloss: Papyrus P46 proves Christians collected letters honoring Jesus Christ around 200 AD.

learn.shortStory: Deep in Egypt, a careful scribe dipped his reed pen in ink, copying John's Gospel line by line. When he made an error, he painstakingly corrected it in the margin. Today, Papyrus P66 reveals the exact same Gospel message of Jesus Christ that we read in our Bibles today.
